Accrual accounting records income and expenses when they happen, not when money changes hands. If you do a job in June and send an invoice, accrual books show the sale in June even if the client pays in July. Similarly, if you get supplies now but pay next month, the cost is recorded now. Cash-basis accounting waits until money actually arrives or leaves your bank: the sale and the bill show up only when you get paid or when you pay.

Accrual gives a clearer picture of how your business is doing over time because it ties work and costs to the same period. Cash basis is simpler and easier to follow since it tracks actual cash flow. Small businesses often use cash basis for simplicity, while businesses that want more complete financial information choose accrual. Choose the one that best fits your size and needs. Talk to your accountant if unsure.
